papers.summary: Defines a behavior-based compression rate for LoRA adapters and finds that weight reconstruction error can misrepresent retained fine-tuning gains.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses low-rank compressibility, singular directions, and corrupted training data.

evidence.quote: near one bit per value, the adaptive code achieves lower relative weight RMSE than uniform quantization (0.54 versus 0.56), yet retains only 3% of the held-out gain, compared with 86% for the uniform code.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Finds contrasting LoRA spectral and subspace dynamics in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, with controlled comparisons implicating group-mean baseline subtraction.
papers.relevance: Connects LoRA optimization to effective rank and singular-subspace motion.

evidence.quote: Controlled comparisons identify group-mean baseline subtraction as a key source of these differences.

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: ResQAdam preserves a QAT momentum residual while compressing optimizer state. Its reported peak-memory savings come with a small throughput decrease versus AdamW.
papers.relevance: Directly informs memory, quality, and speed tradeoffs for low-rank optimizer-state compression.

evidence.quote: This efficiency directly translates to a 15.3% to 19.5% reduction in total peak memory.
The training throughput decreases by less than 2% compared to standard AdamW in all evaluated cases.

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank penalty to LoRA training and reports lower mean Wiki perplexity at tested ranks of at least 16.
papers.relevance: Tests whether spectral regularization can change adapter rank utilization without substantially worsening the training objective.

evidence.quote: a penalty weight of λ = 0.01 \\lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: GEAR uses the normal spectrum to guide LoRA rank expansion and reports an improved LLaMA3-8B commonsense score with fewer trainable parameters.
papers.relevance: Addresses the geometry and practical behavior of dynamically ranked LoRA updates.

evidence.quote: On LLaMA3-8B, it raises the average commonsense score from 86.61 to 88.45 while reducing trainable parameters from 42.0M to 14.4M.

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

papers.summary: Shows that low stable rank need not mean that an LLM weight update is well represented by a small number of singular components.
papers.relevance: Clarifies which spectral rank measures are useful when judging low-rank compressibility.

evidence.quote: Three attention updates from proximal policy optimization (PPO) have stable ranks 9.6 9.6 – 18.3 18.3 but require 532 532 – 1,222 1{,}222 components for 80 % 80\\% of their energy.

papers.title: Spectral Rank and Step-Direction Dynamics in Language-Model Post-Training

papers.summary: Finds delayed validation-loss benefits from temporary weight decay in Muon pretraining across four tested model scales.
papers.relevance: Informs optimization-schedule evaluation and scale-dependent quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Matched intervention and reference runs share initialization, data order, and learning-rate schedule.
A 10% decay window starting at initialization beats both no decay and the best sampled constant at every scale (Table 1 ).

papers.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining

papers.summary: In a quadratic two-layer model, finite Newton–Schulz depth changes early rank selection and can bypass a gradient-flow stationary point.
papers.relevance: Provides a theoretical connection between Muon’s approximation depth and rank dynamics, not yet an LLM-training result.

evidence.quote: In a quadratic two-layer network, we have characterized the evolution from small-initialization escape near the origin to the first nonzero stationary stage.

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

papers.summary: Studies distributed Muon-style spectral updates, finite Newton–Schulz orthogonalization, and low-rank momentum communication. Its measured compression tradeoff is on a small vision benchmark.
papers.relevance: Addresses convergence and communication costs of matrix-valued optimization.

evidence.quote: rank- 32 32 compression reduces the simulated communication payload by 40.5 % 40.5\\% , from 385.39 to 229.34 GB.

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee

papers.summary: SCALAR trains scalar coefficients over fixed bases and reports lower peak memory and higher throughput than LoRA for Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Offers a measured parameter-efficient fine-tuning alternative for memory and throughput comparisons.

evidence.quote: SCALAR achieves the lowest peak memory among the evaluated PEFT methods, using 20% less memory than LoRA, 15% less than NOLA, and 33% less than RandLoRA.
Training throughput increases by 6% over LoRA

papers.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

papers.summary: Uses active learning to approximate LLM document reranking at a controlled evaluation budget; its strongest reported result is for verbose queries.
papers.relevance: Potentially useful for reducing LLM calls in a paper-retrieval pipeline.

evidence.quote: For verbose queries, LAAM achieves 87% of average P@10 achieved by DeepSeek’s reranking (0.459 vs. 0.526), while requiring only 3.3% of the per-query energy consumption.

papers.title: Active Learning of Approximate LLM Ranking for Energy-Efficient Retrieval of Long Queries

papers.summary: Studies query-specific reranking depth and reports that an LLM-assessed first-stage quality measure can reduce average depth while preserving effectiveness.
papers.relevance: Could inform how deeply a digest agent reranks candidate papers.

evidence.quote: IR-DCG@10 , can reduce the average re-ranking depth by up to a factor of 3 while preserving overall effectiveness, depending on the specific first- and second-stage rankers used.

papers.title: Optimal Re-Ranking Depth

papers.summary: Proposes selecting agent memories by estimated decision utility rather than semantic relevance alone.
papers.relevance: A possible design idea for context selection in the research-digest agent, though evaluated in other agent settings.

evidence.quote: semantic relevance is used only for high-recall candidate generation, while predicted utility arbitrates which memories are retained under a fixed token budget

papers.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents

papers.summary: Surveys information-seeking decisions in LLM systems, including retrieval routing, query refinement, tool exploration, and evidence use.
papers.relevance: Maps directly onto decisions required by a tool-using research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: Existing studies report gains in retrieval routing, query refinement, multi-tool exploration, evidence-grounded reasoning, and resource-aware search

papers.title: From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models

papers.summary: Analyzes Muon training dynamics for next-token prediction in Transformers and reports convergence and spectral-margin results.
papers.relevance: Connects matrix optimization theory to language-model training.

evidence.quote: For the main phase, we establish nonasymptotic convergence rates for the training loss and the normalized margin gap under softmax attention.

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of Muon on Transformers for Next-Token Prediction
